_note: Значения сверены с международными рекомендациями (см. sources). Перед релизом утверждаются клиническим руководителем под протокол отделения.

sources.acidBase: Boston rules: Narins & Emmett, Medicine 1980; Berend, Rev Clin Esp 2018 (Winters, metabolic alkalosis 0.7×HCO3+21, respiratory 0.1/0.35, 0.2/0.4). Copenhagen SBE: Schlichtig, Crit Care Med 1998.
sources.anionGap: Kraut & Madias, Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2007; albumin correction 0.25 mmol/L per g/L: Figge, Crit Care Med 1998. Delta ratio: Rastegar, J Am Soc Nephrol 2007.
sources.osmolarGap: Kraut & Kurtz, Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2008 (gap > 10 mOsm/kg).
sources.stewart: Fencl et al., Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2000; Story et al., Br J Anaesth 2004 (simplified: Na−Cl−38, 0.25×(42−albumin), −lactate).
sources.adultARDS: ARDS Definition Task Force (Berlin), JAMA 2012; global ARDS definition (S/F ≤ 315 with SpO2 ≤ 97%): Matthay et al., Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2024.
sources.pediatricARDS: PALICC-2: Emeriaud et al., Pediatr Crit Care Med 2023 (OI ≥ 16 / OSI ≥ 12 severe; SpO2 ≤ 97% for OSI).
sources.neonatalOI: AAP/ELSO: iNO consideration OI > 25, ECMO OI > 40 (Kinsella et al.; ELSO Neonatal Respiratory Failure Guidelines 2017).
sources.preterm: European Consensus Guidelines on RDS — 2022 update (Sweet et al., Neonatology 2023): SpO2 target 90–94%, moderate hypercapnia acceptable with pH ≥ 7.22.
sources.cord: ACOG Committee Opinion 348 / 2014 Neonatal Encephalopathy: pH < 7.0 and/or BE ≤ −12 pathological acidaemia. Therapeutic hypothermia criteria A: pH ≤ 7.0 or BE ≤ −16; pH 7.01–7.15 or BE −10…−15.9 require additional criteria (TOBY/NICHD, NICE IPG347, BAPM 2020).
sources.bicarbonate: ILCOR/NRP 2020: no routine sodium bicarbonate in neonatal resuscitation; 4.2% (0.5 mmol/mL), slow infusion. Lactic acidosis: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021 (no bicarbonate if pH ≥ 7.2); BICAR-ICU, Lancet 2018 (pH ≤ 7.20). DKA: ADA 2024 consensus (bicarbonate only if pH < 7.0).
sources.lactate: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021: lactate ≥ 2 hyperlactataemia, ≥ 4 high risk.
sources.analyzer: Radiometer ABL800 FLEX Reference Manual, ch. 6 Derived parameters: cHCO3-(P) — actual bicarbonate (use for Boston rules); cHCO3-(P,st) — standard; cBase(Ecf) = SBE; mOsm,c is calculated (not for osmolar gap); FiO2 = pO2 / [pO2(a)/FO2(I)].
sources.haemoglobin: WHO 2024 Guideline on haemoglobin cut-offs to define anaemia (6–23 mo <105, 24–59 mo <110, 5–11 y <115, 12–14 y <120, women <120, men <130 g/L); neonatal ranges: Nathan & Oski / Harriet Lane. Transfusion: TOP trial (Kirpalani, NEJM 2020) restrictive arm; children TAXI/TRIPICU 70 g/L; adults AABB 2023 (Carson, JAMA 2023): 70 g/L, 75 cardiac surgery, 80 orthopaedic surgery or cardiovascular disease.
sources.cooximetry: COHb: non-smoker < 3%, smoker ≤ 10%; hyperbaric oxygen to consider at COHb > 25% (> 15–20% in pregnancy) or neurological signs (ACEP 2017, UHMS). MetHb: normal < 2%, cyanosis ~10–15%, methylene blue 1–2 mg/kg if > 20% with symptoms or > 30% (avoid in G6PD deficiency).
sources.potassiumCorrection: Hypokalaemia grades 3.0–3.4 / 2.5–2.9 / < 2.5. Neonates and children IV KCl: max 0.2 mmol/kg/h (0.5 in ICU with ECG), ≤ 40 mmol/L peripheral, ≤ 80 central (NSW Neonatal ANMF; PCH Perth). Adults ≤ 10 mmol/h peripheral, 20 mmol/h central (UK SPC). Check Mg2+.
sources.calcium: Ionised Ca: term and unstable preterm treat < 1.1, stable preterm < 0.8 (RCH Melbourne; Worcestershire NHS); children and adults < 1.0 significant, < 0.8 severe. Calcium gluconate 10% 0.5 mL/kg (50 mg/kg) over 5–10 min with ECG (RCH Neonatal Medication Guidelines), max 20 mL; adults 10–20 mL over 10 min.
sources.bilirubin: ≥ 35 weeks: AAP 2022 (Kemper et al., Pediatrics 2022;150:e2022058859) hour-specific nomogram — use the AAP tool (bilitool.org); escalation of care within 34 µmol/L of the exchange threshold. < 35 weeks: Maisels et al., J Perinatol 2012 operational thresholds by GA (lower end with risk factors).
sources.glucose: Neonates: BAPM 2017 (< 1.0 IV; < 2.0 act; < 2.5 with signs), PES 2015 (> 2.8 mmol/L first 48 h, > 3.3 after 48 h); hyperglycaemia > 8.3, insulin to consider > 14 (NICE NG154). Children: ISPAD level 1 < 3.9, level 2 < 3.0; DKA glucose > 11 with pH < 7.3 or HCO3 < 18 (ISPAD 2022). Adult ICU target 7.8–10, insulin > 10 (NICE-SUGAR, ADA).
sources.lactateAge: Adults SSC 2021 ≥ 2 / ≥ 4; children ≥ 2 (SSC paediatric 2020). Neonates: up to ~4 normal in the first 6 h, > 2.5 persistent is concerning; cord lactate > 6.2 associated with neurological abnormality.
sources.venousSample: Byrne et al., Respirology 2014: venous pH −0.03…−0.04, pCO2 +4.4 mmHg, HCO3 +1. Arterial-labelled sample likely venous: pO2 < 40–45 mmHg with sO2 < 75–80%, or sO2 vs SpO2 gap > 10%.
sources.deficits: Total body water: ~0.8 L/kg preterm, ~0.75 term (Friis-Hansen 1961), 0.6 children and adult men, 0.5 adult women. Na deficit = TBW × (target − Na), rise ≤ 8 mmol/L per 24 h; free water deficit = TBW × (Na/140 − 1), fall ≤ 10 mmol/L per 24 h (Adrogué & Madias, NEJM 2000). Cl deficit = 0.2 L/kg × weight × (100 − Cl) in chloride-responsive metabolic alkalosis (Rose & Post).
sources.extended: SBE (Van Slyke) = 0.93 × (HCO3 − 24.4 + 14.83 × (pH − 7.4)) — the equation behind cBase(Ecf) (Siggaard-Andersen; CLSI C46). Expected pH: acute ΔpH = 0.008 × ΔpCO2, chronic 0.003. Corrected HCO3 = HCO3 + (AG − 12) (Wrenn 1990). Expected AG ≈ 0.25 × albumin g/L (Feldman 2005). Strong ion gap: SIDe = HCO3 + albumin × (0.123·pH − 0.631) + Pi × (0.309·pH − 0.469); SIG = SIDa − SIDe (Figge 1992; Kellum 2009). Na−Cl difference 32–40, Cl:Na 0.75–0.79 (Durward 2001). Na corrected for glucose +2.4 per 5.55 mmol/L (Hillier 1999). cCa2+(7.4) = cCa2+ × 10^(−0.24 × (7.4 − pH)) (Radiometer / Siggaard-Andersen). a/A ratio > 0.75 (Gilbert & Keighley 1974). Shunt from the content equation with C(a−v)O2 2.3 mmol/L = 5.15 mL/dL (Radiometer FShunt,e); normal < 10%. Expected PaO2 = 104.2 − 0.27 × age (Sorbini 1968). Dead space Vd/Vt = (PaCO2 − PetCO2)/PaCO2 (Enghoff), normal 0.2–0.35, > 0.6 high risk in ARDS (Nuckton 2002). Temperature: pH(T) = pH − 0.0147 × (T − 37); pCO2(T) = pCO2 × 10^(0.019 × (T − 37)). Bilirubin/albumin ratio (mg/dL per g/dL) for exchange consideration: ≥ 38 wk 8.0 (7.2 with risk factors); 35–37 wk 7.2 (6.8 with risk) — AAP 2004/2022. Oxygen dissociation: Severinghaus 1979 S = 1/(23400/(P³+150P)+1), p50 = 26.86 mmHg; virtual pO2 = pO2 · 10^(0.024(37−T) + 0.40(pH−7.4) + 0.06·log(40/pCO2)) (Kelman 1966); in-vivo p50 from one point = 26.86 · pO2 / P_std(sO2); normal p50 24–29 mmHg. PIO2 = FiO2 × (Patm − 47). FO2Hb = sO2 × (1 − FCOHb − FMetHb). Bicarbonate deficit by HCO3 (Kassirer): 0.5 × weight × (24 − HCO3). Maintenance fluid (Holliday & Segar 1957): 4/2/1 mL/kg/h.
sources.perfusion: CvO2 = 1.39 × Hb × ScvO2 + 0.003 × pvO2; a–v O2 difference 3–5 mL/dL; O2ER = (CaO2 − CvO2)/CaO2, normal 0.22–0.32; ScvO2 ≥ 70% (Rivers 2001; SSC); shunt Qs/Qt = (CcO2 − CaO2)/(CcO2 − CvO2) (Berggren); DO2 = CO × CaO2 × 10, VO2 = CO × (CaO2 − CvO2) × 10; venous–arterial pCO2 gap > 6 mmHg = low flow (Vallet 2013; Mallat 2016).
sources.ventilation: Ventilation index VI = RR × PIP × PaCO2 / 1000 (neonatal, Notter); driving pressure = Pplat/PIP − PEEP, > 15 cmH2O associated with mortality (Amato, NEJM 2015); ventilatory ratio = VE × PaCO2 / (PBW × 100 × 37.5), > 2 associated with mortality (Sinha 2019); PBW = 50 + 0.91 × (height − 152.4) (ARDSNet, male formula; female 45.5 + …).
sources.series: Na correction speed: rise ≤ 8 mmol/L and fall ≤ 10 mmol/L per 24 h (Adrogué & Madias; European hyponatraemia guideline 2014). Lactate clearance ≥ 10% within 2–6 h (Nguyen 2004; Jones 2010).

bilirubinAAP2022._note: Таблицы AAP 2022 (Kemper et al., Pediatrics 2022;150:e2022058859, Supplemental Tables 1–4) вносятся сюда как точки [час жизни, мкмоль/л] по неделям гестации 35…40 (40 = ≥ 40 нед). Пока таблицы не внесены и не сверены, приложение не принимает решение для ≥ 35 нед и отсылает к номограмме AAP.
